questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The body system made up of bones, providing structural support and protection for internal organs, is called the
questions.explanation: The skeletal system provides the body's structural framework, protecting internal organs and supporting movement in conjunction with muscles.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A joint that allows movement in only one plane, similar to the action of a door hinge, such as the elbow or knee, is called a
questions.explanation: Hinge joints, such as the elbow and knee, allow movement in a single plane, similar to the back-and-forth motion of a door hinge.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A joint that allows movement in multiple directions, formed by a rounded bone end fitting into a cup-shaped socket, such as the hip or shoulder, is called a
questions.explanation: Ball-and-socket joints, found at the hip and shoulder, allow a wide range of movement in multiple directions.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The tough, flexible connective tissue that cushions joints and gives shape to structures like the ear and nose is called
questions.explanation: Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue that cushions joints and provides structural support in areas like the ears and nose.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The strong, fibrous connective tissue that attaches bone to bone, stabilising joints, is called a
questions.explanation: Ligaments connect bone to bone, providing stability and preventing excessive movement at a joint.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The strong, fibrous connective tissue that attaches muscle to bone, allowing movement when the muscle contracts, is called a
questions.explanation: Tendons connect muscles to bones, transmitting the force of muscle contraction to produce movement at a joint.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A postural defect characterised by an excessive outward (rounded) curvature of the upper spine is called
questions.explanation: Kyphosis is an abnormal, excessive outward curvature of the upper spine, sometimes referred to as a 'hunchback' posture.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A postural defect characterised by an excessive inward curvature of the lower spine is called
questions.explanation: Lordosis is an abnormal, excessive inward curvature of the lower (lumbar) spine, sometimes called 'swayback'.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A postural defect characterised by an abnormal sideways curvature of the spine is called
questions.explanation: Scoliosis is an abnormal sideways curvature of the spine, which can develop during childhood growth spurts.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A key corrective habit for preventing postural defects is to
options: carry heavy bags on only one shoulder every day
avoid all forms of physical activity entirely
always slouch when sitting for long periods
maintain correct sitting and standing posture, and avoid carrying heavy loads unevenly
questions.explanation: Maintaining good posture and avoiding uneven heavy loads are key habits that help prevent the development of postural defects over time.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The muscular organ responsible for pumping blood throughout the body is the
questions.explanation: The heart is the muscular pump at the centre of the circulatory system, driving blood throughout the body.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Blood vessels that carry oxygenated blood away from the heart to the rest of the body are called
questions.explanation: Arteries carry oxygen-rich blood away from the heart to tissues throughout the body (with the exception of the pulmonary artery).

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Blood vessels that carry deoxygenated blood back toward the heart are called
questions.explanation: Veins return deoxygenated blood back toward the heart (with the exception of the pulmonary vein).

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The smallest blood vessels, where the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products occurs between blood and body tissues, are called
questions.explanation: Capillaries are tiny, thin-walled vessels where the actual exchange of gases, nutrients, and waste occurs between blood and surrounding tissues.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The straw-coloured liquid component of blood, in which blood cells are suspended, is called
questions.explanation: Plasma is the liquid portion of blood, carrying nutrients, hormones, and waste products, and suspending the blood's various cells.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Red blood cells, responsible for transporting oxygen throughout the body, are called
questions.explanation: Erythrocytes (red blood cells) contain haemoglobin, which binds and transports oxygen throughout the body.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: White blood cells, primarily responsible for defending the body against infection, are called
questions.explanation: Leukocytes (white blood cells) form a key part of the immune system, defending the body against infections and foreign invaders.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Small cell fragments in the blood responsible for clotting to stop bleeding are called
questions.explanation: Platelets are small cell fragments that clump together and initiate blood clotting to prevent excessive bleeding after an injury.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The organ primarily responsible for filtering waste products from the blood and producing urine is the
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter waste products and excess substances from the blood, producing urine to be eliminated from the body.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The tiny functional filtering units within the kidney, responsible for producing urine, are called
questions.explanation: Nephrons are the microscopic filtering units within each kidney, responsible for processing blood and producing urine.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The largest internal organ, responsible for functions including detoxification, bile production, and nutrient processing, is the
questions.explanation: The liver performs numerous vital functions, including detoxifying harmful substances, producing bile, and processing nutrients absorbed from digestion.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Waste products and excess water are also eliminated from the body through small openings in the skin called
questions.explanation: Skin pores release sweat, which helps eliminate certain waste products and excess water, while also regulating body temperature.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A gland located at the base of the brain, often called the 'master gland' because it regulates many other endocrine glands, is the
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland is often called the 'master gland' because its hormones regulate the activity of many other endocrine glands in the body.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A gland located in the neck that regulates the body's metabolic rate through hormone production is the
questions.explanation: The thyroid gland produces hormones that regulate the body's overall metabolic rate.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A gland that produces insulin, a hormone essential for regulating blood glucose levels, is the
questions.explanation: The pancreas produces insulin, a hormone that helps regulate blood glucose levels by facilitating its uptake into cells.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Glands located above each kidney, responsible for producing hormones involved in the stress response, are the
questions.explanation: The adrenal glands, situated above the kidneys, produce hormones such as adrenaline, central to the body's stress response.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The basic functional unit of the nervous system, responsible for transmitting electrical and chemical signals, is called a
questions.explanation: Neurons are specialised cells that transmit electrical and chemical signals throughout the nervous system.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: An automatic, involuntary response to a stimulus, occurring without conscious thought, is called a
questions.explanation: Reflex actions are rapid, automatic responses to stimuli that occur without requiring conscious thought, such as pulling a hand away from something hot.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Good personal hygiene of the skin generally involves
options: applying substances that clog pores intentionally
never changing clothing regardless of activity
avoiding all forms of washing to preserve natural oils
regular washing to remove dirt, sweat, and dead skin cells
questions.explanation: Regular washing helps maintain healthy skin by removing dirt, excess sweat, and dead skin cells, reducing the risk of skin problems.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Good dental hygiene generally involves
options: regular brushing and flossing to remove food particles and plaque
avoiding brushing entirely to protect tooth enamel
consuming only sugary foods with no other dietary considerations
questions.explanation: Regular brushing and flossing help remove food particles and plaque, preventing tooth decay and gum disease.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Good eye care generally involves
options: rubbing the eyes vigorously with dirty hands
staring directly at bright light sources for extended periods
ignoring any changes in vision indefinitely
protecting the eyes from strain and injury, and having regular check-ups
questions.explanation: Protecting the eyes from strain, injury, and harmful exposure, along with regular check-ups, supports good long-term eye health.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Good ear care generally involves
options: exposing the ears to extremely loud noise without protection
keeping the outer ear clean and avoiding inserting sharp objects into the ear canal
ignoring any pain or discharge from the ear indefinitely
regularly inserting sharp objects deep into the ear canal
questions.explanation: Gently cleaning the outer ear and avoiding inserting objects into the ear canal helps prevent injury and infection.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Good hand hygiene, particularly regular handwashing, is important mainly because it
options: is only necessary once a week
helps prevent the spread of germs and infectious disease
increases the spread of germs significantly
has no effect on disease transmission at all
questions.explanation: Regular handwashing is one of the most effective ways to reduce the spread of germs and prevent infectious disease transmission.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Good foot care generally involves
options: ignoring any foot pain or injury indefinitely
wearing ill-fitting shoes regardless of comfort
avoiding all forms of foot hygiene
keeping feet clean and dry, and wearing properly fitting footwear
questions.explanation: Keeping feet clean, dry, and properly protected with well-fitting footwear helps prevent infections and other foot problems.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The system responsible for coordinating rapid responses to stimuli using electrical signals throughout the body is the
questions.explanation: The nervous system coordinates rapid responses to internal and external stimuli using electrical and chemical signals transmitted through neurons.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A disease-causing microorganism, such as a virus, bacterium, fungus, or protozoan, is called a
questions.explanation: A pathogen is any microorganism capable of causing disease, including viruses, bacteria, fungi, and protozoa.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: An organism, such as a mosquito, that transmits a pathogen from one host to another is called a
questions.explanation: A vector, such as the Anopheles mosquito for malaria, transmits disease-causing pathogens between hosts.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Malaria is caused by a parasite belonging to the genus Plasmodium, transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected
questions.explanation: Malaria is transmitted through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito, which carries the Plasmodium parasite.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A common symptom of malaria includes
options: instant, painless recovery with no symptoms
questions.explanation: Malaria commonly presents with recurring fevers, chills, headache, and general body weakness.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A key method for controlling the spread of malaria is
options: encouraging stagnant water collection near homes
avoiding all forms of mosquito control measures
using insecticide-treated bed nets and eliminating mosquito breeding sites
questions.explanation: Insecticide-treated bed nets and eliminating stagnant water (mosquito breeding sites) are key strategies for controlling malaria transmission.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Typhoid fever is caused by a type of bacteria, transmitted mainly through
questions.explanation: Typhoid fever is caused by Salmonella typhi bacteria, primarily transmitted through consumption of contaminated food or water.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A key preventive measure against typhoid fever is
options: ensuring safe drinking water and proper food hygiene
ignoring proper handwashing after using the toilet
drinking untreated water from any available source
questions.explanation: Safe drinking water and good food hygiene practices are essential in preventing the transmission of typhoid fever.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Tuberculosis is caused by a bacterium primarily affecting the
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis primarily affects the lungs, though it can also affect other body organs in some cases.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Tuberculosis is mainly transmitted through
options: airborne droplets from an infected person's cough or sneeze
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis spreads mainly through airborne droplets released when an infected person coughs or sneezes.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Cholera is caused by a bacterium that leads to severe diarrhoea and dehydration, transmitted mainly through
questions.explanation: Cholera bacteria spread mainly through water and food contaminated with faecal matter from infected individuals.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A key treatment for cholera, addressing its most dangerous immediate effect, is
options: withholding all fluids from the patient
administering only pain relief medication with no rehydration
oral rehydration therapy to replace lost fluids and salts
questions.explanation: Oral rehydration therapy addresses the severe dehydration caused by cholera, replacing the fluids and salts lost through diarrhoea.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Measles is a highly contagious viral disease primarily transmitted through
options: airborne droplets and direct contact with infected respiratory secretions
questions.explanation: Measles spreads through airborne droplets and direct contact with respiratory secretions from an infected person.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A key preventive measure against measles is
options: exposing unvaccinated children intentionally to infected individuals
questions.explanation: Routine immunisation is highly effective at preventing measles and is a cornerstone of childhood vaccination programmes.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) primarily attacks and weakens the
questions.explanation: HIV attacks the immune system, progressively weakening the body's ability to fight infections, and can lead to AIDS if untreated.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: HIV can be transmitted through
options: casual contact such as hugging or shaking hands
unprotected sexual contact, contaminated blood, and mother-to-child transmission
sharing meals with an infected person
questions.explanation: HIV transmission occurs through specific routes, including unprotected sexual contact, contaminated blood, and from mother to child, but not through casual everyday contact.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are generally best prevented through
options: avoiding all forms of protection during sexual activity
safe sexual practices, including the correct use of condoms
ignoring symptoms of any infection indefinitely
sharing personal items with infected individuals
questions.explanation: Safe sexual practices, including consistent and correct condom use, significantly reduce the risk of transmitting sexually transmitted infections.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Diseases that develop gradually and are generally not caused by an infectious pathogen, such as hypertension and diabetes, are classified as
questions.explanation: Non-communicable diseases, such as hypertension, diabetes, and many cancers, are not caused by infectious agents and generally develop over a longer period.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Hypertension (persistently high blood pressure) is a significant risk factor for
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled hypertension significantly increases the risk of serious complications, including stroke and various forms of heart disease.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Diabetes mellitus is a condition characterised by the body's inability to properly regulate
options: oxygen levels in the blood only
questions.explanation: Diabetes mellitus involves the body's impaired ability to regulate blood glucose levels, due to problems with insulin production or use.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Sickle cell anaemia is an inherited condition affecting the shape and function of
questions.explanation: Sickle cell anaemia is a genetic condition causing red blood cells to become abnormally shaped, impairing their ability to carry oxygen effectively.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Cancer is generally characterised by
options: an entirely reversible condition requiring no medical attention
a purely psychological condition with no physical basis
the uncontrolled growth and division of abnormal cells
questions.explanation: Cancer involves the uncontrolled growth and division of abnormal cells, which can invade surrounding tissues and spread throughout the body.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Asthma is a chronic condition primarily affecting the
questions.explanation: Asthma causes inflammation and narrowing of the airways, leading to breathing difficulties, wheezing, and coughing.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Access to pure, clean drinking water in a community is important mainly to
options: increase the spread of waterborne disease intentionally
prevent waterborne diseases such as cholera and typhoid
have no meaningful impact on community health
replace the need for proper sanitation entirely
questions.explanation: Clean drinking water is essential for preventing waterborne diseases such as cholera and typhoid within a community.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Proper sewage processing within a community is important mainly to
options: prevent contamination of water sources and reduce disease transmission
eliminate the need for any clean water supply
increase the risk of disease transmission intentionally
have no effect on public health outcomes
questions.explanation: Effective sewage processing prevents human waste from contaminating water sources, reducing the risk of disease transmission within a community.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Effective solid waste disposal strategies in a community help to
options: increase the accumulation of disease-carrying pests
have no bearing on community health or environment
eliminate the need for any environmental regulation
reduce breeding sites for disease vectors and prevent environmental pollution
questions.explanation: Proper solid waste disposal reduces breeding sites for pests and vectors, helping to prevent both disease transmission and environmental pollution.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Atmospheric (air) pollution control measures are important mainly to
options: eliminate the need for community health education
reduce respiratory illnesses and protect overall community health
increase the prevalence of respiratory illness intentionally
have no significant impact on public health
questions.explanation: Controlling air pollution helps reduce the incidence of respiratory illnesses and supports the overall health of a community.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The international organisation primarily responsible for coordinating global public health matters is the
options: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
questions.explanation: The WHO is the United Nations agency specifically responsible for coordinating international public health efforts and policy.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The international organisation primarily focused on protecting the rights and wellbeing of children worldwide, including health initiatives, is
questions.explanation: UNICEF focuses specifically on protecting children's rights and wellbeing globally, including health, nutrition, and education initiatives.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The Nigerian regulatory agency primarily responsible for the safety and quality of food and drugs is
questions.explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) regulates the safety and quality of food, drugs, and related products in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Fungal infections are among the pathogens studied in relation to communicable disease because they can cause conditions such as
questions.explanation: Fungal pathogens are responsible for various infections, including ringworm and athlete's foot, distinct from bacterial or viral diseases.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A key approach to resolving conflicts in a healthy manner is to
options: avoid all communication and let tension build indefinitely
communicate openly and seek mutually acceptable solutions
respond with immediate aggression in every situation
refuse to consider the other party's perspective at all
questions.explanation: Healthy conflict resolution involves open communication and a genuine effort to find solutions acceptable to all parties involved.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A healthy technique for managing stress includes
options: regular physical activity, relaxation techniques, and adequate rest
avoiding all forms of physical activity and rest
increasing substance use to cope with stress
ignoring stress indefinitely without any coping strategy
questions.explanation: Effective stress management often combines regular physical activity, relaxation techniques, and sufficient rest to help the body and mind cope with pressure.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Managing psychological anxiety in a healthy way often involves
options: relying solely on harmful substances to cope
isolating oneself completely from all social support
seeking support from trusted individuals or professionals when needed
questions.explanation: Seeking appropriate support from trusted individuals or mental health professionals is an important, healthy strategy for managing persistent anxiety.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Puberty is generally characterised by
options: physical, hormonal, and emotional changes marking the transition to sexual maturity
changes that occur only in early childhood
no physical changes of any kind
a permanent halt in physical growth and development
questions.explanation: Puberty involves significant physical, hormonal, and emotional changes as an individual transitions from childhood toward sexual maturity.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The menstrual cycle refers to the
options: single event occurring only once in a lifetime
process unrelated to female reproductive health
monthly hormonal and physiological process preparing the female body for potential pregnancy
process exclusive to male reproductive physiology
questions.explanation: The menstrual cycle is a recurring monthly process involving hormonal changes that prepare the female body for potential pregnancy.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Fertilization occurs when
options: two egg cells combine without any sperm involvement
no biological process takes place at all
a sperm cell fails to reach any egg cell
a sperm cell successfully unites with an egg (ovum) cell
questions.explanation: Fertilization is the biological process in which a sperm cell unites with an egg cell, forming the beginning of a new individual.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Antenatal care refers to the
options: care provided only to newborn infants
care unrelated to pregnancy or childbirth
healthcare provided to a woman during pregnancy to monitor her health and that of the developing baby
questions.explanation: Antenatal care involves regular healthcare check-ups during pregnancy, monitoring the health of both the mother and the developing foetus.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Immunization timelines for children are important mainly to
options: eliminate the need for any future healthcare visits
ensure vaccines are given at the optimal age for effective protection against disease
delay all forms of disease protection indefinitely
have no bearing on a child's health outcomes
questions.explanation: Following recommended immunization timelines ensures children receive vaccines at ages when they are most effective in providing protection against disease.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Family planning methods are generally used by couples to
options: make informed choices about the timing and number of children they have
avoid any consideration of family health and resources
increase the risk of unintended pregnancy intentionally
eliminate any choice regarding family size
questions.explanation: Family planning allows couples to make informed decisions about when to have children and how many, considering health, resources, and personal circumstances.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: When evaluating health-related advertisements, consumers should generally
options: critically assess claims rather than accepting them without question
accept all claims made in an advertisement without any scrutiny
ignore any concerns about a product's safety or efficacy
avoid seeking any further information about a product
questions.explanation: Critically evaluating health advertisements, rather than accepting claims uncritically, helps consumers make safer, more informed decisions.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Checking a food or drug product's expiry date before use is important mainly to
options: have no bearing on the product's safety
avoid consuming products that may have degraded or become unsafe
guarantee the product will remain safe indefinitely regardless of date
increase the shelf life of the product artificially
questions.explanation: Checking expiry dates helps consumers avoid using products that may have degraded in quality or become unsafe for consumption.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Food adulteration refers to the
options: process of enriching food with beneficial nutrients only
addition of harmful, inferior, or non-declared substances to food products
process of properly preserving food using approved methods
labelling of food products with accurate ingredient information
questions.explanation: Food adulteration involves adding harmful or inferior substances to food, often to reduce costs or increase quantity deceptively, posing health risks to consumers.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A balanced nutrient profile in one's diet is important mainly to
options: eliminate the need for any variety in food choices
have no bearing on overall health outcomes
support overall health and prevent nutrient deficiencies or excesses
guarantee immunity from all forms of disease
questions.explanation: Maintaining a balanced nutrient profile supports overall health and helps prevent both nutrient deficiencies and the health risks of excessive intake.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: The use of a drug for its intended medical purpose, as prescribed, is generally described as
questions.explanation: Drug use refers to taking a substance for its intended, legitimate medical purpose, typically as prescribed or recommended.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Using a drug in a way not intended or recommended, such as taking a higher dose than prescribed, is generally described as
questions.explanation: Drug misuse refers to using a substance in a manner not intended or recommended, such as exceeding the prescribed dosage.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A condition in which an individual has developed a strong physical or psychological need to continue using a drug is called
questions.explanation: Drug dependency (addiction) describes a strong physical or psychological compulsion to continue using a substance, often despite negative consequences.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Excessive alcohol consumption can have significant physiological effects, including damage to the
questions.explanation: Excessive alcohol consumption can cause significant damage to organs such as the liver, as well as harmful effects on the nervous system.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Tobacco use is strongly associated with an increased risk of
options: improved lung function with no health risks
lung cancer and other respiratory diseases
reduced risk of all forms of cancer
questions.explanation: Tobacco use significantly increases the risk of lung cancer and various other respiratory diseases, among other serious health effects.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Stimulant drugs generally have the physiological effect of
options: increasing alertness, heart rate, and energy levels temporarily
inducing immediate, deep sleep in all users
having no effect on the nervous system at all
permanently curing anxiety with no side effects
questions.explanation: Stimulant drugs typically increase alertness, heart rate, and perceived energy levels temporarily, though often with significant health risks.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Narcotic drugs generally have the physiological effect of
options: reducing pain perception and inducing sedation, with significant risk of dependency
increasing alertness and physical energy dramatically
having no impact on pain perception whatsoever
guaranteeing complete safety with no risk of dependency
questions.explanation: Narcotics reduce pain perception and induce sedation, but carry a significant risk of dependency and other serious health consequences with misuse.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A structured process designed to help individuals overcome substance dependency and return to healthy functioning is called
questions.explanation: Rehabilitation programmes provide structured support to help individuals overcome substance dependency and rebuild healthy, functional lives.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A key step in supporting someone recovering from substance dependency is
options: ignoring the individual's need for any form of assistance
providing consistent emotional support and encouraging professional treatment
isolating the individual completely from all support systems
encouraging continued substance use to avoid withdrawal symptoms
questions.explanation: Consistent emotional support, alongside encouragement to pursue professional treatment, plays a vital role in helping individuals recover from substance dependency.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Emotional health is best described as a state in which an individual can generally
options: experience only positive emotions with no capacity for difficulty
avoid any form of social interaction entirely
manage their emotions constructively and maintain healthy relationships
questions.explanation: Good emotional health involves the ability to manage emotions constructively, cope with challenges, and maintain healthy relationships with others.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: During puberty, hormonal changes in males typically lead to
options: deepening of the voice and growth of facial hair
no physical changes of any kind
a permanent halt in physical growth
the onset of the menstrual cycle
questions.explanation: Puberty in males is typically marked by hormonal changes leading to physical developments such as voice deepening and facial hair growth.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: During puberty, hormonal changes in females typically lead to
options: growth of facial hair as the primary change
the onset of the menstrual cycle and breast development
no physical changes of any kind
deepening of the voice as the primary change
questions.explanation: Puberty in females is typically marked by hormonal changes leading to physical developments such as the onset of menstruation and breast development.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Tracking one's menstrual cycle can be useful mainly for
options: understanding fertility patterns and planning for family planning or pregnancy
predicting unrelated illnesses with no connection to reproduction
eliminating the need for any healthcare visits
questions.explanation: Tracking the menstrual cycle helps individuals understand their fertility patterns, which can support family planning decisions or efforts to conceive.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A key component of antenatal care is
options: avoiding all medical check-ups until after childbirth
regular monitoring of the mother's and baby's health throughout pregnancy
ignoring any warning signs of complications during pregnancy
discontinuing all forms of prenatal nutrition
questions.explanation: Antenatal care involves regular check-ups to monitor the health and development of both mother and baby throughout the course of pregnancy.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Common family planning methods include
options: barrier methods, hormonal methods, and natural methods
options limited to a single universal method for all couples
approaches that ignore individual health considerations entirely
methods that guarantee an identical outcome for every couple
questions.explanation: Family planning encompasses a range of methods, including barrier methods (like condoms), hormonal methods, and natural methods, allowing couples to choose what suits their needs.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A key sign of healthy stress management is the ability to
options: remain in a state of heightened stress indefinitely
ignore the physical symptoms of stress entirely
recover and return to a balanced emotional state after a stressful event
avoid all forms of stress permanently, in every situation
questions.explanation: Healthy stress management is reflected in the ability to recover and return to emotional balance after experiencing a stressful event, rather than remaining in prolonged distress.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Peer pressure can influence young people to engage in substance abuse mainly through
options: an absence of any social interaction
a desire for social acceptance or fear of exclusion from a group
questions.explanation: Peer pressure often influences behaviour through a desire for social acceptance or fear of being excluded from a social group, which can contribute to risky behaviours like substance abuse.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A key long-term health consequence of chronic alcohol abuse is
options: enhanced physical fitness with no downsides
questions.explanation: Chronic alcohol abuse can lead to serious long-term liver damage, including cirrhosis, a scarring of liver tissue that impairs its function.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: Family life education aims mainly to
options: discourage all forms of family formation
ignore the importance of reproductive health entirely
eliminate the need for any health education
prepare individuals for responsible relationships, parenting, and family roles
questions.explanation: Family life education helps prepare individuals for responsible relationships, parenting, and the various roles and responsibilities within family life.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A healthy coping strategy for managing grief or loss includes
options: avoiding any acknowledgement of the loss indefinitely
suppressing all emotions related to the loss permanently
turning to substance abuse as the primary coping method
seeking support from family, friends, or counselling services
questions.explanation: Seeking support from trusted family, friends, or professional counselling is a healthy strategy for coping with grief and loss.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A community health worker's role in reproductive health education often includes
options: providing no information related to reproductive health
focusing exclusively on unrelated economic issues
educating individuals and families about antenatal care, family planning, and safe childbirth practices
discouraging any form of healthcare engagement
questions.explanation: Community health workers often play a key role in educating individuals and families about important reproductive health topics, including antenatal care and family planning.

questions.subject: Health Education
questions.text: A key aspect of building resilience in emotional health is
options: avoiding every possible challenge or setback in life
relying entirely on others to manage all personal difficulties
developing effective coping strategies to adapt to adversity and setbacks
questions.explanation: Resilience involves developing effective coping strategies that allow an individual to adapt positively in the face of adversity and setbacks.
